reuse.why: Reuses recurrence conversion and date adjustment helpers, but separately implements occurrence policy in the upcoming, range and budget consumers.

duplication.why: Daily skip policy, weekend-or-holiday detection and adjustment dispatch remain repeated across shared and server code.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs appropriately in shared schedules, but server handlers and the budget module also own scheduling policy.

scope.why: All edits directly support the requested scheduling rules, range handler and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several independently expressed occurrence policies and consumer-specific enumeration assumptions when scheduling rules change.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange implement occurrence policy outside shared getNextDate; both budget enumeration calls disable its adjustment and use a local wrapper.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily skip-versus-adjust decision appears as a loop in getNextDate, filtering and mapping in getUpcomingDates, and flatMap branches in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and two budget enumeration sites independently apply occurrence policy.
